title: Do Political Differences Inhibit Market Transactions? An Investigation in the Context of Online Lending
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Single event: California Supreme Court same-sex-marriage ruling, May 15, 2008.
eligible_reason: Single-date design. The DiD (Tables 5-7, 11, 12) is built around one event (California's same-sex-marriage ruling on May 15, 2008; readme.docx): xtset state_listing_dyad period; xtreg total_bids_all period_m3 period_m2 period_p0-period_p3 treated_post_treatment [aweight=cem_weights], fe, with treated = listings by California borrowers and periods indexed relative to the ruling. One adoption date, CEM weights in most columns, Poisson columns, and political-distance x treatment interactions in Table 7. The other main analysis is a cross-sectional state-dyad gravity model (Tables 1-3, 8, 9).
design_notes: replication.do with Replication_Gravity.csv (state dyads), Replication_DID.csv (listing x investor-state x period around May 15, 2008), Replication_Listing.csv (listing-level funding and loan performance) and table-specific robustness files. Table 5 col 1 is unweighted xtreg fe with period dummies (single-date 2x2 event window); cols 2 and 4 CEM-weighted; cols 3-4 xtpoisson.

specs.exclusion_reason: single adoption date (one event), not staggered

data_access_note: Prosper.com public data (2006-2011) plus public ideology and census data; all analysis files shipped.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (abstract from data/frame/mnsc.jsonl).
